full_judgment:
6. Mr. Md. Jahangir slam, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioners submits that the High Court Division misreading and misinterpreting the material points on record and relevant laws of the case in question most wrongly and without applying judicial mind passed the judgment and order occasioning a serious failure of justice which is not at all sustainable in law. He further submits that the High Court Division having not properly perused the materials on record and on misdirecting themselves from the facts and circumstances of the case most wrongly passed the impugned order which is non-judicial and arbitrary and not in the light of the facts and circumstances of the case. He finally submits that the High Court Division miserably failed to take into consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and material points of the case record and under misconception as to facts most wrongly and non-judicially passed the impugned judgment and order which is not at all sustainable in law. 

 9. The writ petitioner's case is that their name was duly included in the list of MPO and that they have been receiving Government portion of salary regularly till October, 2007. Subsequently, without citing any reason or issuing notice whatsoever by the Government, their MPO had suddenly and abruptly been stopped from 01.11.2007 till date. They unsuccessfully submitted appropriate representation to the writ respondents concern to look into the matter and to release their MPO. Finding no other efficacious alternative remedy they filed the instant writ petition seeking direction upon the writ respondents for making payment of their salary and allowances under MPO of the Government. 

 13. The High Court Division in making the Rule absolute considered the Janabal Kathamo of 2010 which has no retrospective application and, as such, not applicable for this case as praying for the MPO from the year 2007. Thus, committed error in passing the impugned judgment.
